text: Now here's a discovery that's genuinely mind-bending. Scientists at UCSF have figured out how our brain cells create unique identities despite having identical genetic instructions. They've discovered that DNA can fold like origami in different patterns, creating billions of unique barcodes for each neuron.

speaker: alice
text: It's like every brain cell has its own fingerprint, Alex, and these patterns have to last for decades since neurons live as long as we do. The researchers reckon if they can understand this process properly, we might be able to rewire faulty brain circuits in conditions like autism and Alzheimer's.

speaker: charlie
text: And just to round out the science goodness, MIT researchers have found that leucine - that's the stuff in your protein-rich tucker - can literally supercharge your cellular power plants by protecting the energy-producing proteins inside. Your Sunday morning eggs are basically giving your cells a turbo boost.
